note: The published view of Beman's conservatory for Pullman across 18th Street from the house: a glass nave on a pointed section with a broad arched frame at its north end over a band of upright glazing and a stone podium with an arched entrance; a transept whose north face rises upright and turns level at a crest; a ribbed dome with a finial on a glazed drum over the crossing; behind at left a one-storey masonry range with a row of square windows ending in a domed colonnade, and a two-storey stone lodge with a bowed front and a crested mansard roof. T-3179 solved its camera (data/reference_views/pullman_glasshouse_1800_calumet_pavilion/inland_1894_conservatory.json) and worked the glasshouse records to it.
what_it_supplies: the conservatory's sections, heights and openings through its camera (49.5 px/m on the north front)
the east range's masonry face, windows and coping height, and its round end's colonnade and dome
the north range's north end as a low curved glass roof
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 state: the plate is 1892-94, and the 1911 sheet draws a longer north range than it shows
the south and west sides, and the ranges' roofs behind their parapets
